subject: English
title: Arun and Maya Find Opposite Words
hook: Explore the fun world of opposites with Arun and Maya!

slides.title: Opposites: Words That Are Totally Different
Hot and Cold are Opposites
slides.storyContext: Arun touches hot tea and says 'Hot!' Maya drinks cold water and says 'Cold!' They're opposite!

points.label: Opposites
points.text: Words that mean completely different things

slides.inSimpleWords: Hot and cold are opposite words!

image.alt: Hot and Cold are Opposites — Opposites

slides.title: What Does Opposite Mean?

points.label: Opposite words
points.text: Two words that mean the exact opposite

points.label: Example pair
points.text: Hot is the opposite of cold

slides.inSimpleWords: Opposites are words that mean the very opposite thing!

slides.title: Big and Small
slides.storyContext: Maya shows a big watermelon and a small grape. 'Big and small are opposites!', she says.

points.label: Big ↔ Small
points.text: These words mean completely opposite sizes

slides.inSimpleWords: Big and small are opposite size words!

image.alt: Big and Small — Opposites

slides.title: Big and Small in Our World

example.problem: What is the opposite of big?
example.solution: Small is the opposite of big

slides.inSimpleWords: Big things are not small, and small things are not big!

slides.title: Happy and Sad
slides.storyContext: Arun laughs and feels happy. But when he loses his toy, he feels sad!
slides.inSimpleWords: Happy and sad are opposite feelings!

image.alt: Happy and Sad — Opposites

slides.title: Feeling Opposites
slides.inSimpleWords: Happy and sad are opposite emotions!

slides.title: Fast and Slow
slides.storyContext: Arun runs very fast! Maya walks very slowly. They move opposite ways!
slides.inSimpleWords: Fast and slow are opposite speed words!

image.alt: Fast and Slow — Opposites

slides.title: Speed Challenge

example.problem: Which is the opposite: fast or slow?
example.solution: Slow is the opposite of fast

slides.inSimpleWords: Slow moves are the opposite of fast moves!

slides.title: Light and Dark, Day and Night
slides.storyContext: When the sun rises, it's light and day. When it sets, it's dark and night!
slides.inSimpleWords: Light and dark, day and night are opposites!

image.alt: Light and Dark, Day and Night — Opposites

slides.title: Day is Light, Night is Dark
slides.storyContext: Maya explains: 'During day, the sun shines bright. During night, there's darkness all around!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Day brings light, night brings dark!

slides.title: More Opposite Pairs
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya play an opposites matching game!

example.problem: Find opposite words: tall, clean, old, young, wet
example.solution: short, dirty, new, old (pair), dry — opposites found!

slides.inSimpleWords: Different words can mean complete opposites!

image.alt: More Opposite Pairs — Opposites

slides.title: Clean and Dirty
slides.inSimpleWords: Clean is the opposite of dirty!

slides.title: More Opposite Words
slides.storyContext: Arun says: open/closed, loud/quiet, left/right, up/down!
slides.inSimpleWords: Positions and actions have opposite words too!

image.alt: More Opposite Words — Opposites

slides.title: Open and Closed
slides.inSimpleWords: Open and closed are opposite states!

slides.title: Position Opposites

example.problem: Give the opposite: up, left, in, outside
example.solution: down, right, out, inside

slides.inSimpleWords: Position words have clear opposites!

slides.title: Find the Opposite Pair

example.problem: Which pair shows opposites? bright-dark or bright-yellow?
example.solution: bright-dark are opposites. bright-yellow are both colors.

slides.inSimpleWords: Opposites are totally different, not just different colors!

slides.title: Tall and Short
slides.storyContext: Arun is tall and Maya is short. They're opposite heights!
slides.inSimpleWords: Tall and short describe opposite heights!

slides.title: Old and New

points.label: Old
points.text: Been around for a long time

slides.inSimpleWords: Old things are from the past, new things are recent!

slides.title: Loud and Quiet
slides.storyContext: At the playground, Arun shouts LOUD! In the library, Maya whispers very quietly!
slides.inSimpleWords: Loud and quiet are opposite sound words!

slides.title: Opposite Matching Challenge

example.problem: Match: cheap, empty, dangerous, wet / full, expensive, safe, dry
example.solution: cheap-expensive, empty-full, dangerous-safe, wet-dry

slides.inSimpleWords: Find all the opposite pairs!

slides.title: Why Learn Opposites?
slides.inSimpleWords: Opposites help us express ideas clearly!

slides.title: Wet and Dry
slides.storyContext: After playing in rain, Arun's clothes are wet. After sun-drying, they become dry!
slides.inSimpleWords: Wet and dry are opposite water words!

slides.title: Opposites in Sentences

example.problem: Use opposites: 'The day is hot...' (use opposite of hot)
example.solution: 'The day is hot, but the night is cold.' Using opposites shows comparison!

slides.inSimpleWords: Use opposites to compare and contrast!

slides.title: Create Your Own Opposites

example.problem: Think of 3 opposite pairs you use every day
example.solution: Examples: morning-night, start-stop, smile-frown, win-lose

slides.inSimpleWords: Opposites are all around us!

slides.title: Strong and Weak
slides.storyContext: Arun shows his strong muscles. Maya shows a weak, delicate flower.
slides.inSimpleWords: Strong and weak describe opposite strengths!

slides.title: Begin and End
slides.inSimpleWords: Begin and end are opposite actions in time!

slides.title: Opposites Everywhere
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write their favorite opposite pairs on the wall!
slides.inSimpleWords: Opposite words mean completely different things!

image.alt: Opposites Everywhere — Opposites

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Rhyme Time
hook: Discover the magic of words that sound the same at the end!

slides.title: What Are Rhyming Words?
slides.storyContext: Arun sings 'cat' and Maya sings 'bat'. They sound the same at the end!

points.label: Rhymes
points.text: Words that sound the same at the end

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyming words sound the same at the end!

image.alt: What Are Rhyming Words? — Rhyming Words

slides.title: How Do Rhymes Work?
slides.inSimpleWords: Rhymes happen when ending sounds match!

slides.title: Cat, Hat, Bat, Rat
slides.storyContext: Arun lists words: cat, hat, bat, rat. They all rhyme because they end the same way!

points.label: 'at' rhyme family
points.text: cat, hat, bat, rat, mat, fat, sat

slides.inSimpleWords: Cat, hat, bat all rhyme together nicely!

image.alt: Cat, Hat, Bat, Rat — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Find the Rhyme Family

example.problem: Which word rhymes with 'cat'? hat, dog, mat, log
example.solution: hat and mat rhyme with cat (all end in -at sound)

slides.inSimpleWords: Words that end the same way rhyme!

slides.title: Dog, Fog, Log, Hog
slides.storyContext: Maya shows: dog, fog, log, hog. All end with 'og' sound!

points.label: 'og' rhyme family
points.text: dog, fog, log, hog, bog, clog

slides.inSimpleWords: Dog, fog, log rhyme with the 'og' sound!

image.alt: Dog, Fog, Log, Hog — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Rhyme Families

points.label: What is a rhyme family?
points.text: A group of words with the same ending sound

points.label: Examples
points.text: -at: cat, bat, hat; -og: dog, fog, log

slides.inSimpleWords: Groups of rhyming words are called rhyme families!

slides.title: Sun, Run, Fun, Bun
slides.storyContext: Arun jumps and shouts: 'Rhyming is fun! I like to run and eat a bun!'

points.label: 'un' rhyme family
points.text: sun, run, fun, bun, gun, nun, stun

slides.inSimpleWords: Sun, run, fun rhyme with the 'un' sound!

image.alt: Sun, Run, Fun, Bun — Rhyming Words

slides.title: More Rhyme Families

example.problem: What rhymes with 'bee'? tree, cat, see, dog
example.solution: tree and see rhyme with bee (all end in -ee sound)

slides.inSimpleWords: Many words can belong to the same rhyme family!

slides.title: Make Rhyming Pairs
slides.storyContext: Maya teaches: take a word and find another word that rhymes with it!

points.label: Finding rhymes
points.text: Listen to the last sounds and match them

slides.inSimpleWords: Find words that end with the same sound!

image.alt: Make Rhyming Pairs — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Make Your Own Rhyme Pairs

example.problem: Find a rhyme pair: ___ and ___
example.solution: Examples: cat-hat, sun-fun, dog-log, tree-bee

slides.inSimpleWords: You can make rhyme pairs from any words!

slides.title: Creating Rhyming Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya make a rhyming sentence together!

example.problem: Make a rhyming sentence with 'cat' and 'hat'.
example.solution: 'The cat wore a hat.' Cat and hat rhyme!

slides.inSimpleWords: Use rhyming words to make fun sentences!

image.alt: Creating Rhyming Sentences — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Rhymes in Stories

points.label: Why use rhymes?
points.text: Rhymes make stories fun and memorable

points.label: Rhyming pattern
points.text: Same ending sounds create a pattern

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyming words make stories more fun!

slides.title: Rhyming Words in Poems
slides.storyContext: Maya recites: 'Roses are red, violets are blue.' The words rhyme and sound beautiful!

points.label: Poems
points.text: Poems often use rhyming words to sound pretty

slides.inSimpleWords: Poems use rhyming words to sound nice!

image.alt: Rhyming Words in Poems — Rhyming Words

slides.title: A Simple Rhyming Poem

example.problem: Make a short rhyming poem with sun and fun
example.solution: 'I like the sun, / It is so fun!' — sun and fun rhyme!

slides.inSimpleWords: Simple poems use just a few rhyming words!

slides.title: Complete the Rhyme

example.problem: The cat sat on the ___. (rhyme with 'cat')
example.solution: mat, hat, bat — any word rhyming with cat works!

slides.inSimpleWords: Fill in words that rhyme to complete sentences!

slides.title: Different Rhyme Patterns
slides.inSimpleWords: Poems can have different rhyme patterns!

slides.title: Rhyming Games
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya play a rhyming game where they take turns finding new rhymes!

points.label: Rhyming game
points.text: One person says a word, the other finds a rhyme

slides.inSimpleWords: Playing rhyming games helps you learn!

slides.title: Rhyming in Nursery Rhymes

example.problem: Humpty Dumpty sat on a ___, Humpty Dumpty had a great ___
example.solution: wall, fall — these rhyme!

slides.inSimpleWords: Nursery rhymes are full of rhyming words!

slides.title: Find All the Rhymes

example.problem: List all words that rhyme with 'moon': June, spoon, balloon, sun
example.solution: June, spoon, balloon all rhyme with moon (end in -oon sound)

slides.inSimpleWords: Some rhyme families have many words!

slides.title: Bee, See, Tree, Sea
slides.storyContext: Maya sings about the bee, see, tree, and sea all rhyming together!

points.label: 'ee' rhyme family
points.text: bee, see, tree, sea, key, tea, free, three

slides.inSimpleWords: The -ee sound creates lots of rhyming words!

slides.title: The Power of Rhyming

points.label: Memory helper
points.text: Rhymes help you remember things better

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyming makes words easier to remember!

slides.title: Rain and Pain, Train and Brain
slides.storyContext: Arun shows the 'ain' rhyme family with words like rain, pain, train, and brain!

points.label: 'ain' rhyme family
points.text: rain, pain, train, brain, gain, main, strain

slides.inSimpleWords: Many words rhyme with the 'ain' sound!

slides.title: Rhyming Helps You Write Better

points.label: Add beauty
points.text: Rhyming makes your writing sound nicer

points.label: Tell a story
points.text: Rhymes help tell stories that stay in memory

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyming words make better stories!

slides.title: Create a Rhyming Pair

example.problem: Make your own rhyming pair and use it in a sentence
example.solution: Examples: 'I like the night / Stars shine so bright' (night-bright rhyme)

slides.inSimpleWords: You can create your own rhyming words!

slides.title: Rhyming Words Everywhere
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write their own rhyming poem together!

points.label: Definition
points.text: Rhyming words sound the same at the end

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyming words sound alike and make poems fun!

image.alt: Rhyming Words Everywhere — Rhyming Words

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Noun and Pronoun Journey
hook: Learn how nouns name things and pronouns replace them!

slides.title: Nouns and Pronouns: The Words That Name and Replace
What is a Noun?
slides.storyContext: Arun points: 'Look! A dog, a tree, a house! These are all nouns — they name things!'

points.label: Noun
points.text: A word that names a person, place, animal, or thing

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns are words that name people, places, things!

image.alt: What is a Noun? — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Four Types of Nouns
slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name four kinds: people, places, animals, things!

slides.title: Nouns Name People
slides.storyContext: Maya lists: 'Arun, teacher, doctor, mother — these are nouns for people!'

points.label: Person nouns
points.text: boy, girl, teacher, doctor, mother, farmer, police

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns that name people are person words!

image.alt: Nouns Name People — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Identify Person Nouns

example.problem: Which are person nouns? dog, teacher, book, mother, tree
example.solution: teacher and mother are person nouns

slides.inSimpleWords: Find the nouns that name people!

slides.title: Nouns Name Places
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'Delhi, school, park, temple — these are places. All nouns!'

points.label: Place nouns
points.text: city, school, park, temple, library, garden, beach

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns that name places are place words!

image.alt: Nouns Name Places — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Place Nouns Around You

example.problem: Name 3 place nouns in your town
example.solution: school, market, park, temple, hospital, library

slides.inSimpleWords: Places you visit are all nouns!

slides.title: Nouns Name Animals and Things
slides.storyContext: Maya points to things: 'Dog, cat, book, pencil, chair — all nouns!'

points.label: Animal and thing nouns
points.text: dog, cat, bird, book, pencil, chair, table, toy

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name animals and objects too!

image.alt: Nouns Name Animals and Things — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Singular and Plural Nouns

points.label: Plural noun
points.text: More than one: books, cats, dogs

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns can be one or many!

slides.title: What is a Pronoun?
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'Instead of saying Arun every time, I say I or me. That's a pronoun!'

points.label: Pronoun
points.text: A word that replaces a noun

slides.inSimpleWords: Pronouns replace nouns in sentences!

image.alt: What is a Pronoun? — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: I, You, He, She, It, We, They
slides.storyContext: Maya teaches the main pronouns: 'I am Maya. You are my friend. He is Arun. She/It/We/They too!'

points.label: Personal pronouns
points.text: I, you, he, she, it, we, they

slides.inSimpleWords: I, you, he, she, it, we, they are pronouns!

image.alt: I, You, He, She, It, We, They — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Using Pronouns Instead of Nouns
slides.storyContext: Arun shows how to replace nouns with pronouns!

example.problem: Maya likes books. Maya reads books. Maya writes about books.
example.solution: Maya likes books. She reads them. She writes about them. (She replaces Maya, them replaces books)

slides.inSimpleWords: Use pronouns to avoid repeating the noun!

image.alt: Using Pronouns Instead of Nouns — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Pronoun Replacement

example.problem: Replace the noun: 'Arun plays football. Arun is fast.'
example.solution: 'Arun plays football. He is fast.' (He replaces Arun)

slides.inSimpleWords: Replace nouns with pronouns to improve writing!

slides.title: My, Your, His, Her, Our, Their
slides.storyContext: Maya says: 'This is my pencil. That is your book. This is his toy. That's her doll.'

points.label: Possessive pronouns
points.text: my, your, his, her, its, our, their

slides.inSimpleWords: Possessive pronouns show who owns something!

image.alt: My, Your, His, Her, Our, Their — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Possessive Pronouns Show Ownership
slides.inSimpleWords: Possessive pronouns tell us who something belongs to!

slides.title: Using Possessive Pronouns

example.problem: Fill in: This is Arun's book. This is ___ book. (use possessive pronoun)
example.solution: This is his book. (his is the possessive pronoun for Arun)

slides.inSimpleWords: Use possessive pronouns to show ownership!

slides.title: Identify Nouns and Pronouns

example.problem: Find the noun and pronoun: 'Maya is smart. She loves reading.'
example.solution: Noun: Maya, reading. Pronoun: She

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name, pronouns replace!

slides.title: Why Do We Use Pronouns?

points.label: Avoid repetition
points.text: Don't repeat the same noun over and over

slides.inSimpleWords: Pronouns make writing easier and clearer!

slides.title: Subject and Object Pronouns
slides.storyContext: Arun explains: 'I kick the ball. The ball hits me. In first case, I is the subject. In second, me is the object.'

points.label: Subject pronouns
points.text: I, you, he, she, it, we, they (do the action)

points.label: Object pronouns
points.text: me, you, him, her, it, us, them (receive the action)

slides.inSimpleWords: Subject pronouns do the action, object pronouns receive it!

slides.title: Subject vs Object Pronouns

example.problem: Fill in: ___ (subject) gave the book to ___ (object).
example.solution: 'She gave the book to him.' (She is subject, him is object)

slides.inSimpleWords: Use the right pronoun in the right place!

slides.title: Pronoun Detective

example.problem: Identify every noun and pronoun: 'Arun met Maya. He gave her a gift.'
example.solution: Nouns: Arun, Maya, gift. Pronouns: He, her

slides.inSimpleWords: Find all the nouns and pronouns in a sentence!

slides.title: Proper Nouns: Special Names
slides.storyContext: Maya explains: 'Arun is a person's name. Names always start with a capital letter. They're called proper nouns!'

points.label: Proper nouns
points.text: Special names that start with capital letters: Arun, Maya, Delhi, India

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of specific people and places need capital letters!

slides.title: Proper Nouns vs Common Nouns

example.problem: Which is proper? 'boy' or 'Arun'
example.solution: 'boy' is common. 'Arun' is proper because it's a name.

slides.inSimpleWords: Proper nouns name specific things!

slides.title: Demonstrative Pronouns
slides.inSimpleWords: Demonstrative pronouns point to things!

slides.title: This and That
slides.storyContext: Arun points: 'This is my book. That is Maya's book over there.'

points.label: This/That
points.text: Point to one thing close or far

points.label: These/Those
points.text: Point to more than one thing

slides.inSimpleWords: Use this/that/these/those to point to things!

slides.title: Nouns and Pronouns
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya create a chart showing nouns and their pronoun replacements!

points.label: Pronouns
points.text: I, you, he, she, it, we, they (replace nouns)

points.label: Possessives
points.text: my, your, his, her, our, their (show who owns)

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name. Pronouns replace. Both are important!

image.alt: Nouns and Pronouns — Nouns and Pronouns
